chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding the salat (prayer) of the day is reciting quietly, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding the salat (prayer) of the night is reciting aloud.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the normative prophetic practice and prescribed manner

ai.seo_question: What is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) for reciting in daytime and nighttime salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states the sunnah (prophetic tradition) for recitation in supererogatory prayers: daytime salat (prayer) is to be performed with quiet recitation, while nighttime salat (prayer) is with audible recitation. It presents a legal guideline in the etiquette and manner of worship.
